messages.subject: version 0.9-1 released
messages.body_plain:
Greetings,

unmarked_0.9-1 was just submitted to CRAN and soon will be available for download on all platforms. Along with a few minor bug fixes, there are two important additions.

First, there is a new function, gdistsamp, to fit a generalized form of the Royle et al. (2004) distance sampling model. This expanded model relaxes the assumption that g(0)=1 by including an additional parameter psi, the probability of being available for detection. This should be useful for studies where cues such as bird songs or whale blows are counted. The gdistsamp function also allows abundance to be modeled using the negative binomial distribution. See Chandler et al. (Ecology 2011) for more details about this model.

The other new addition is a vignette on dynamic occupancy models (MacKenzie et al. 2003) . Marc Kéry deserves most of the credit for putting this together. Thanks Marc! In addition to helping with the implementation of colext(), this vignette describes many of unmarked's basic features such as data manipulation, prediction, model selection, etc...

More information about this release can be found here: https://sites.google.com/site/unmarkedinfo/home/release-notes

Richard

_____________________________________
Richard Chandler, post-doc
USGS Patuxent Wildlife Research Center

messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

 it was a pleasure to help write  the vignette about colext(). Richard helped me with the code quite a bit (Thanks, Richard !) and for this, and also, especially, for developing the very useful unmarked package, I was happy to contribute something in exchange.

As you may see in this vignette, it contains a quite verbose description of the capabilities of colext. I think that having extensive worked examples is essential for letting many ecologists apply statistical analyses for their own data sets. In the longer term, it would be great to have such vignettes for all functions contained in unmarked. A little like Evan Cooch's MARK handbook. So perhaps some of you can have a try at writing something about their own favourite function in unmarked.

Thanks again, Richard (and Ian and Andy), for giving unmarked to the world.

Kind regards  --  Marc

messages.body_plain:
Hi Mike,

That sure is a worthless error message -- I'll make a note to fix it. It's hard to know exactly what the problem is without knowing the dimensions of the matrices you imported. Can you show the results of:

str(data.y)
str(data.obsCovs)
str(data.siteCovs)

data.y should have 8 columns and one row per site. The order of the columns should be something like: "obs1visit1, obs2visit1, obs1visit2, etc..."

data.siteCovs should also have one row per site and each column should be a covariate.

There are several ways to format obsCovs, but let's ignore that for the moment.

Once your data is set up correctly, you need to specify numPrimary=4.

Another issue that needs to be addressed is that type="removal" assumes that you used the "independent" double observer method. I'll make sure to add that to the documentation. Since you want the "dependent" method, you will have to supply a user-defined "piFun". I can help with that, but could you first try to run your code again with the data formatted as described above?

Richard

messages.body_plain:
So there were only 2 visits, not 4? In that case, please try the code below, which includes an appropriate "piFun" and "obsToY" matrix.

depDoubleObs <- function(p) {
    M <- nrow(p)
    pi <- matrix(NA, M, 2)
    pi[,1] <- p[,1]
    pi[,2] <- p[,2]*(1-p[,1])
    return(pi)
}

obsToY <- matrix(1, 2, 2)
numPrimary <- 2
obsToY <- kronecker(diag(numPrimary), obsToY)

umfGMM <- unmarkedFrameGMM(y=data.y, siteCovs=data.siteCovs,
  obsCovs=data.obsCovs, numPrimary=2, obsToY=obsToY,
   piFun="depDoubleObs")
(m1 <- gmultmix(~1,~1,~1, data=umfGMM))

I realize that the obsToY matrix is confusing, but, the great thing about this function and multinomPois() is that the user can create their own function for computing multinomial cell probs. Thus you can tailor the function to your study design as we are doing here. obsToY just tells the function how the covariates "map" to the counts. THere are more details about this scattered around the help files.

Keep us posted.

Richard

messages.subject: fitted values from colext?
messages.body_plain:
Greetings,
Thanks for a great R package (unmarked) and a very helpful google
group!

I'm having trouble extracting fitted values from a colext model.  I'd
like to use the fitted values in a parametric bootstrap to examine
goodness of fit (following the example on pg. 16 in the dynamic
occupancy model vignette).

When I run the following colext example code:

# Real data
data(frogs)
umf <- formatMult(masspcru)
obsCovs(umf) <- scale(obsCovs(umf))
## Use 1/4 of data just for run speed in example
umf <- umf[which((1:numSites(umf)) %% 4 == 0),]
## constant transition rates
(fm <- colext(psiformula = ~ 1,
gammaformula = ~ 1,
epsilonformula = ~ 1,
pformula = ~ JulianDate + I(JulianDate^2), umf, control =
list(trace=1, maxit=1e4)))
fitted(fm)

I get the following error message:

Error in .local(umf, ...) :
  unused argument(s) (formlist = list(psiformula = ~1, gammaformula =
~1, epsilonformula = ~1, pformula = ~JulianDate + I(JulianDate^2)))

Any ideas what might be going wrong?
Thanks,
Steve
